title: Chapter 106: Hensheng: To Hate Life 9
content:
Chapter 106

Hensheng: To Hate Life 9

"What letter?" Lan Xichen asked.

"A threat," Jin Guangyao replied. "Spelling out… everything. The sender gave me seven days before dragging it all into the daylight. My choices were to slit my own throat to make amends, or… sit around waiting for them to put me in the dirt."

The pieces clicked into place for everyone listening. Of course someone like Jin Guangyao wasn't going to sit around twiddling his thumbs, waiting for an executioner. Rather than watch his reputation burn while the entire cultivation world laughed him out of existence, he chose a preemptive strike. If his purge had succeeded, it wouldn't have mattered what filthy laundry came out later; battered and hollowed out from a bloodbath, no one would have had the strength left to challenge him.

Too bad his luck ran out the second Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji crashed the party.

"Even so, you can't just go scorched-earth and slaughter everyone!" Lan Xichen’s voice cracked with frustration. "Pulling something like this..."

You aren't even leaving me room to defend you!

"Then tell me, what was I supposed to do?" Jin Guangyao fired back. "Sit on my hands until the scandal blew up, wait until I became the single greatest joke in the cultivation world for the next century, and then drop to my knees, put my face in the dirt, and beg them to step on my neck and grant me mercy? Er-ge! There wasn't a middle ground. It was their heads or mine."

A flash of genuine temper flickered across Lan Xichen's face as he took a sharp step back. "And whose fault is that?! It’s because you actually did the monstrous things in that letter! If you hadn't done them, who could have ever held leverage over your head?"

"Er-ge, listen to me," Jin Guangyao pleaded. "I'm not denying any of it—"

"How could you even try?" Lan Xichen cut him off. "The witnesses are breathing right in front of us!"

"Which is why I'm owning up to it! But slaughtering a father, a wife, a child, a sworn brother—do you honestly believe I'd do that unless I was backed completely into a corner? Am I really that far gone, that much of a bloodthirsty lunatic in your eyes?"

Lan Xichen forced his breathing to level out, clamping down on his agitation. "Fine. I have a few questions for you. You're going to answer them, one by one."

"Brother!" Lan Wangji warned.

Bichen cleared its scabbard with a crisp hiss. Catching the lethal intent rolling off his brother, Lan Xichen held up a hand. "Don't worry. He's injured and stripped of his weapons; he's cornered and outnumbered. With this many eyes on him, he can't pull anything." Right on cue, Wei Wuxian sent Su She sprawling with a swift kick, snuffing out the man’s attempt to pull something shady in the background. Lan Xichen added, "Keep an eye on that side. I'll handle him."

Lan Wangji turned toward the commotion, tracking Su She's muffled snarls. Wei Wuxian knew Lan Xichen was still clinging to whatever lingering fondness he held for his sworn brother, nursing some desperate, naive hope that demanded he hear the man out. Luckily, Wei Wuxian had a few burning questions of his own, so he tilted his head, listening closely.

"First," Lan Xichen began, "your father, the former Sect Leader Jin. Did you truly engineer his death... in that manner?"

Jin Guangyao kept his tone cautiously deferential. "May I save that answer for last?"

Lan Xichen let out a pained breath and shook his head, pressing forward. "Second. Your... wife..." The word seemed to stick in his throat, and he corrected himself with bitter revulsion: "Your sister, Qin Su. Did you marry her knowing full well the blood you shared?"

Jin Guangyao stared at him blankly, the fight suddenly draining out of him as tears welled in his eyes.

"...Yes," he choked out.

Lan Xichen took a sharp breath, his face going pale and ashen.

"I didn't have a choice," Jin Guangyao whispered.

"How could you not have a choice?!" Lan Xichen snapped, losing his composure. "It was your wedding! If you hadn't gone through with it, that would have been the end of it! Breaking her heart would have been a mercy compared to dragging down a woman who loved and revered you, who never once looked down on you!"

"And you think I didn't love her back?!" Jin Guangyao’s voice cracked, raw and shrill. "I was cornered! When I say I had no way out, I mean it! Yes, it was my wedding, but do you seriously think I could have just waved it off and called it quits? Er-ge, there’s a limit to how naive you can afford to be! Do you have any idea how much blood and sweat I poured into getting Qin Cangye's blessing? The wedding date was set, both Qin Cangye and Jin Guangshan were ecstatic, and you expected me to drop a bomb and call it off out of nowhere? What excuse could I have possibly given them? How was I supposed to face either of those men?

"Er-ge, do you have any idea what it felt like to have Madame Qin pull me into the shadows and drop that horror on me right when I thought my life was finally falling into place? A bolt of divine lightning striking the crown of my head wouldn't have terrified me more! And do you know why she ran crying to me instead of confronting Jin Guangshan? Because he raped her! That bastard of a father couldn't even keep his hands off the wife of his most loyal subordinate, and he couldn't even remember when he’d sired another daughter! Madame Qin kept that poison buried from her husband for decades. If I had suddenly backed out and tipped off their suspicions, blowing up the alliance between Jin Guangshan and Qin Cangye, who do you think would have been ground to dust between them?!"

Even though everyone in the room knew what an irredeemable scumbag Jin Guangshan had been, hearing it laid out so plainly sent a violent shiver through the hall. Disgust and dread warred for dominance, leaving an acrid taste in the air.

"Even so..." Lan Xichen struggled to find his voice. "Even if your hand was forced into marrying Qin Su, you could have kept your distance. Why did you... Why did you have to bring A-Song into this world, only to turn around and slaughter your own flesh and blood?!"

Jin Guangyao clutched his head in his hands, his voice dropping into a ragged scrape. "...I never touched A-Su after our wedding night. A-Song was... conceived before the vows. I was terrified that things would fall apart if I dragged my feet, terrified of unexpected complications..."

So he had bedded Qin Su ahead of time.

If not for that panicked rush, he wouldn't have blundered into incest with his own half-sister. Sitting in the dirt, it was impossible to tell whether he hated the monster who had fathered him more, or the paranoid, scheming creature he had become.

Lan Xichen let out a long, heavy exhale. "Third. Drop the evasions and answer me cleanly. Jin Zixuan’s death—did you orchestrate it from the start?"

At the mention of his father's name, Jin Ling’s eyes snapped wide, his hands freezing where they held Jiang Cheng steady.

Lan Wangji raised his voice slightly from the side. "Brother, you actually believe him?"

Lan Xichen looked torn, conflict bleeding through his eyes. "I don't for a second believe Jin Zixuan simply stumbled upon the ambush at Qiongqi Path by accident. But... let him speak."

Knowing that a flat-out denial wouldn't hold water, Jin Guangyao gritted his teeth. "...Jin Zixuan being there was not an accident."

Jin Ling’s knuckles turned white as he balled his hands into fists.

"But I never planned the bloodbath that followed," Jin Guangyao rushed to add. "Stop treating me like some all-knowing puppet master playing three steps ahead of fate. So much of that day was entirely out of anyone's hands. How could I have possibly known he would drop dead beside Jin Zixun at Wei Wuxian's hands? How could I have predicted that Wei Wuxian would lose his grip, or that the Ghost General would tear everyone to shreds?"

"Then why the hell did you tip him off in the first place?!" Wei Wuxian snarled. "You’re talking in circles!"

"I'm not denying that I deliberately leaked word of the ambush to him," Jin Guangyao confessed. "All I wanted was to drop him into the middle of your feud, let him get roughed up while dealing with his cousin's mess. How could I have foreseen that you, Master Wei, would go scorched-earth and slaughter every breathing soul on that mountain path?"

Wei Wuxian let out a sharp, incredulous bark of laughter. "You really are something else..."

"Why?!" Jin Ling screamed.

He tore away from Jiang Cheng’s side, eyes bloodshot, and threw himself toward Jin Guangyao. "Why would you do that to him?!"

Nie Huaisang hurriedly lunged forward, grabbing Jin Ling’s robes before the boy could throw a punch.

Jin Guangyao looked up, murmuring, "Why?"

He locked eyes with the boy. "A-Ling, maybe you can answer a question for me instead. Why was it that no matter how much I groveled, no matter how bright I smiled, no one ever gave me the time of day—while your father could walk around with his nose in the clouds and have the entire world tripping over themselves to kiss his boots? Can you tell me why, when we were both sons of the exact same man, your father got to lounge at home playing house with the woman he loved and doting on his son, while I couldn't even bear to spend five minutes alone with my own wife? Why did looking at my own flesh and blood make my skin crawl, while our father casually treated me like an attack dog, sending me to corner a ticking bomb who could massacre an army with a wave of his hand?!

"Why was it that on our shared birthday, Jin Guangshan threw a lavish, decadent banquet to celebrate one son, while standing by and watching his dogs kick his other son down the steps of Koi Tower—from the absolute highest terrace down to the dirt at the bottom?!"

The mask slipped, laying bare a raw, rotting hatred—not aimed at Jin Zixuan, and not aimed at Wei Wuxian, but laser-focused on the man who had sired him.

"Stop looking for excuses!" Wei Wuxian snapped. "If you wanted payback, you should have gone after the man who wronged you! What the hell did Jin Zixuan ever do to you?!"

"And as you can see," Jin Guangyao replied with terrifying calm, "I killed them all."

Lan Xichen’s voice shook. "And you did it through that method."

A tear slipped from the corner of Jin Guangyao’s eye, but he didn't slouch. Kneeling upright with his spine rigid, a faint smile pulled at his lips. "Yes. An old rutting beast that couldn't keep it in his pants deserved an end fitting for a stud, wouldn't you agree?"

"A-Yao!" Lan Xichen barked.

The rebuke slipped out before he could catch himself, a stinging reminder that he had already severed ties and had no right to use that familiar name. Jin Guangyao didn't seem to care, meeting his gaze evenly. "Er-ge, you might hear me spitting venom right now, but I actually held out hope for that man once. I carried out his orders without question—whether it was betraying Sect Leader Wen, sheltering Xue Yang, or butchering political rivals. It didn't matter how idiotic or despised the task was, I did it. But do you want to know the exact moment I stopped caring?

"To answer your very first question: it wasn't because I never mattered as much to him as a single hair on Jin Zixuan's head, or the rot eating away at Jin Zixun. It wasn't because he dragged Mo Xuanyu back, or spent his final years trying to strip away my authority. It was what he told a prostitute while drunkenly carousing one night.

"Why wouldn't a grand, filthy-rich sect leader lift a single finger to buy out my mother’s contract? Simple. Because it was a hassle. My mother wasted her entire life waiting for him, spinning excuses to my face about his grand, unavoidable hardships. And the cold, hard reality boiled down to two pathetic words: too troublesome.

"You want to know his exact words? 'Women who can read a few verses are the worst of the lot. They think they're better than the rest, always making demands and living in their heads. It’s an absolute headache. If I bought her out and let her cling to Lanling, who knows how much she’d pester me? Better to leave her right where she is. With her looks, she can squeeze out a few more good years, and she won't starve in the gutter. As for the kid? Bah, don't even mention him.'"

Jin Guangyao's memory was frighteningly sharp, reciting the drunken rant with eerie accuracy; anyone listening could practically see the leering, sloppy grin plastered across Jin Guangshan’s face. He let out a breathless, airy laugh. "See, Er-ge? My entire existence as his son was worth exactly four words: don't even mention him. Ahahahahaha..."

Lan Xichen looked away, his expression tangled in grief. "Even if your father was monstrous... you still shouldn't have..." He trailed off, the words failing him before he sighed, hollowed out. "What's the point of dredging this up now?"

Jin Guangyao spread his hands with a wet, helpless grin. "Can't help it. Rotten to the marrow, yet still pathetic enough to crave a sliver of sympathy. That’s just who I am, I suppose."

Right as the syllables left his mouth, his wrist snapped.

A scarlet, blood-soaked guqin string whipped through the air, snaring Jin Ling by the throat.

Tears still clung to Jin Guangyao's lashes, but his voice went pitch-black. "Don't move."

The move was lightning-fast. Jiang Cheng bellowed, "Wei Wuxian! Didn't you strip him of his weapons?!"

Pushed to the brink, Jiang Cheng barked out the demand with the exact same frantic snap from their youth. Wei Wuxian yelled back, "I took every single string off him!" The man couldn't have manifested metal out of thin air!

Lan Wangji’s eyes narrowed, instantly seeing through the trick. "It was buried inside his body."

Everyone followed his gaze. A dark, expanding bloom of crimson was spreading across the white silk at Jin Guangyao’s flank. The chord wasn't red by design; it was dripping with fresh gore. Wei Wuxian hadn't found it because it hadn't been tucked into his robes—Jin Guangyao had literally embedded it beneath his own flesh. He had stalled for time, playing on Lan Xichen’s guilt and baiting Jin Ling closer, only digging into his own stomach to rip the weapon free once the boy was within arm's reach.

No one had imagined he would go to such sickening lengths just to keep a contingency play. As thin as the wire was, carrying a coiled hunk of foreign metal lodged in your guts while moving around was nothing short of self-inflicted torture.

"A-Ling!" Jiang Cheng shouted, his voice cracking. Wei Wuxian took an involuntary step forward, only to be yanked back by Lan Wangji's firm grip, anchoring him before he could lose his head.

Jin Guangyao hauled Jin Ling upright, using the boy as a shield. "No need to lose your temper, Jiang-zongzhu. I practically raised A-Ling myself. My offer still stands: let me walk away, and you'll get him back in one piece."

"Don't you dare move, A-Ling!" Jiang Cheng panted, clutching his wound. "Jin Guangyao, if you need a hostage, take me instead!"

"Hard pass," Jin Guangyao replied brightly. "You're bleeding out and can barely walk; you'd only slow me down."

Sweat gathered on Wei Wuxian’s palms. "Jin-zongzhu, aren't you leaving someone behind? Your devoted little attack dog is still on our side of the room."

Jin Guangyao’s gaze flicked to Su She, who was pinned under Bichen's lethal gleam.

Su She wheezed through gritted teeth, "Don't worry about me, Sect Leader!"

"Appreciated," Jin Guangyao shot back without missing a beat.

Lan Xichen spoke, his voice dropping into a flat, icy register. "Jin-zongzhu, you've lied to me once again."

"Just this once, Er-ge," Jin Guangyao murmured. "Never again."

"You said the exact same thing last time. I honestly have no idea if a single word out of your mouth has ever been real."

Jin Guangyao opened his mouth to reply, but an ear-splitting crack of thunder tore through the sky, sounding as if the heavens had split directly above the roof. The shockwave made him flinch, choking the words back down.

THUD. THUD. THUD.

Three deafening, violent impacts battered against the temple doors.

It wasn't a knock. It sounded as though someone had grabbed a corpse by the ankles and was swinging its skull into the wood like a battering ram. With each brutal slam, the iron crossbar groaned, splintering fractures running spiderweb-thin through the timber.

With every impact, the panic twisting Jin Guangyao’s face grew more grotesque.

On the fourth hit, the deadbolt snapped in half. A gust of freezing rain and a tumbling black silhouette blew through the shattered doors simultaneously.

Jin Guangyao flinched, instincts screaming to dodge, but he checked himself just in time. The projectile wasn't aimed at him; it was hurtling straight toward Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji. The pair parted with practiced grace, letting the body fly between them before stepping back shoulder-to-shoulder.

Wei Wuxian glanced behind him. "Wen Ning?"

Wen Ning had slammed headfirst into the Guanyin statue, dangling upside-down like a broken marionette for a second before flopping onto the floorboards with a wet thud. "...Master," he rasped.

Jiang Cheng and Jin Ling's faces darkened the moment they registered the fierce corpse.

Nie Huaisang, however, let out a piercing scream: "Da-ge!!!"

Framed by the ruined doorway stood another figure, hulking and monstrous in the pouring rain. His jaw was set like raw iron, his skin the color of cold lead, and his eyes completely vacant.

Chifeng-zun, Nie Mingjue!

He loomed like an iron fortress in the downpour, cutting off any hope of escape. His severed head sat squarely on his shoulders, held in place by dense, clumsy lines of thick black thread. Someone had crudely stitched his rotting head back onto his headless torso!

"Da-ge..." Lan Xichen breathed, his voice trembling.

"...Da-ge..." Jin Guangyao echoed in a hollow daze.

Three different men calling out to the same corpse, yet their voices carried worlds of difference. Pure, suffocating terror hollowed out Jin Guangyao’s expression, a violent shiver raking through his frame. In life and in death, the single person who had always terrified him to his core was this unyielding, ruthless sworn brother.

His shoulder trembled, his hand slipped, and the crimson string around Jin Ling’s neck began to twitch.

In that split second, Lan Wangji drew Bichen, the blade carving a lethal arc through the dark.

Before anyone could blink, Lan Wangji was already standing in front of Jin Ling, catching something midair.

Jin Guangyao felt his arm go suddenly light. He blinked, glancing down at his sleeve—only to realize his right hand was gone.

Cleanly sheared off at the forearm. The severed hand Lan Wangji had caught still had its bloody fingers clamped around the deadly wire.

A fountain of dark gore sprayed across the floorboards. Shock and agony drained the last scrap of color from Jin Guangyao’s face, robbing him of the breath to even scream. He stumbled backward, his knees buckling until he crumpled to the ground. Su She, however, shrieked in horror. Lan Xichen flinched, an instinctive urge to help twitching in his fingers, but he forced himself to stay rooted to the spot.

Lan Wangji pried open the dead fingers of the severed hand, letting the tension fall out of the wire to free Jin Ling. Jiang Cheng moved to check on the boy, but Wei Wuxian beat him to it, grabbing Jin Ling by the shoulders and rapidly scanning him from collar to chin. Seeing that the skin was unbroken without even a scratch, Wei Wuxian finally let out the breath trapped in his chest.

Lan Wangji rarely struck with such brutal finality, but there had been zero room for hesitation. In the hands of a master assassin, that chord could saw through bone in a blink. Jin Guangyao had been shaking; if his grip had slipped, or if he’d panicked and bolted for the door, Jin Ling’s head would have rolled across the floor before anyone could draw a breath. Lan Wangji’s strike had been the only thing standing between the boy and a gruesome death.

Jin Ling was drenched in the arterial spray from Jin Guangyao's stump, blood painting his face and tunic, frozen in stunned silence.

Wei Wuxian yanked the kid into a fierce, bone-crushing hug. "Next time, stay the hell away from maniacs like him, you idiot! What were you doing standing that close?!"

If Jiang Yanli and Jin Zixuan's only boy had died right in front of him, Wei Wuxian genuinely wouldn't have known how to go on living.

Unused to being held like that, Jin Ling’s pale cheeks flushed bright crimson as he squirmed, shoving frantically against Wei Wuxian’s chest. Wei Wuxian just squeezed him tighter, slapped him hard on the shoulder, and shove-guided him toward Jiang Cheng. "Go on! Quit running off and glue yourself to your uncle!"

Jiang Cheng caught the dazed boy by the arm. Looking across at Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji standing together, he swallowed his pride, muttering a low, rough, "Thank you."

Quiet, but crisp and clear.

Jin Ling echoed him, bowing his head. "Thank you for saving my life, Hanguang-jun."

Lan Wangji gave a slight nod, offering no reply. Bichen angled down, its crystalline edge repelling the crimson droplets until the steel gleamed immaculate once more, before turning to point directly at the giant looming in the doorway.

Across the hall, Wen Ning pushed himself up, casually snapping his dislocated wrist back into its joint with a dull pop. "Be careful..." he rasped, hollow eyes fixed on the shadow. "The malice on him is unlike anything I've ever felt."
